First, we note that:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$
